newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade light $66 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle trade light $66 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle sold at $66.00 per cwt in light volume after midday Tuesday, unchanged from thin sales on Friday, feedlot sources said.
About 1,900 head sold in Kansas, mostly from one feedyard, they said. There were no sales reported in the Texas Panhandle and western Oklahoma area.
Packer bids during the day ranged from $65.00 to $66.00, with most bids passed by owners pricing cattle at $67.00 to $68.00, the feedlot sources said.
Activity was slow following the three-day Memorial Day holiday, with packers well supplied with cattle, they said.
There was concern that cool, wet weather in the central U.S. had dampened beef demand, but several market sources said it could take a few days before holiday beef sales were known.

The Memorial Day holiday is the unofficial start of the summer cookout season and poor weather may have slowed sales, or at least delayed consumption of beef that was bought in anticipation of warm weather, the sources said.
Midday beef sales were anemic, with no indication of strong retail replacement demand. Beef was quoted up $0.03 to $0.20 per cwt, with 49 fabricated loads sold, USDA reported.
